Zaireichthys camerunensis (Daget & Stauch, 1963). Type locality: Bénoué basin at Lakdo, Cameroon. Size: 33 mm (1.3") SL. IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2020).

The majority of species in the genus are small and compact. They have a defence mechanism of three ossified spines in the dorsal and pectoral fins, which they can lock into place; this makes the genus different from all other Amphiliidae.

This species is slender for the genus, with a projecting upper lip and a slightly indented caudal fin with the lower lobe slightly longer. The base colour is light yellow-white, with a row of dark spots on the back and a second longitudinal row of oval dark spots on the mid flank, and a dumb-bell shaped dark area on the caudal fin.
Africa: only in the Niger basin, including the Upper Niger and the Bénoué (Upper Bénoué), in Nigeria and Cameroon.
Characteristically in the wild most Zaireichthys live just above and in fine sand (where they will bury themselves) in flowing water.
Mémoires de l'Institut français d'Afrique Noire No. 68, pp 94, Fig. 1.
